hich wildcard is used to represent zero or more characters in an SQL query?
ChatGPT said:

In an SQL query, the wildcard used to represent zero or more characters is the percent sign (%).

Example:

sql
SELECT * FROM employees
WHERE name LIKE 'Jo%';

This will match:

  • Jo

  • John

  • Joanna

  • Jonathan

The % matches any sequence of characters (including none).

Utilize the SELECT statement to retrieve data from the Expense Tracker database. Apply wildcards (%) and comparison operators for targeted data retrieval. Employ the WHERE clause with logical operators (AND, OR, NOT) to filter data effectively. Organize retrieved data using the ORDER BY clause. Certainly! Here's a sample SQL query that demonstrates the use of:

  • SELECT to retrieve data

  • WHERE with wildcards (%), comparison operators, and logical operators (AND, OR, NOT)

  • ORDER BY to organize the output

Let’s assume the expenses table in your Expense Tracker database has the following columns:

  • id (primary key)

  • description (text)

  • category (text)

  • amount (decimal)

  • expense_date (date)

✅ Sample SQL Query:

sql
SELECT id, description, category, amount, expense_date
FROM expenses
WHERE 
    description LIKE '%food%'             -- wildcard: contains 'food'
    AND amount > 100                      -- comparison: amount greater than 100
    AND category NOT LIKE '%entertain%'   -- NOT operator: exclude categories with 'entertain'
    OR (category = 'Utilities' AND amount <= 300)  -- OR and AND combined
ORDER BY expense_date DESC;              -- organize by most recent expenses first

🔍 Explanation:

  • description LIKE '%food%': selects any description that contains the word "food".

  • amount > 100: filters expenses with an amount over 100.

  • category NOT LIKE '%entertain%': excludes entertainment-related expenses.

  • OR (category = 'Utilities' AND amount <= 300): adds another valid condition group.

  • ORDER BY expense_date DESC: sorts results with the latest expense on top.

  • ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE avoids duplicate id errors during repeated inserts.

You said:
What is the function of a SELECT statement in SQL?
ChatGPT said:

The SELECT statement in SQL is used to retrieve data from one or more tables in a database.

🔍 Function:

It queries the database and returns data in the form of a result set (like a table with rows and columns).

✅ Basic Syntax:

sql
SELECT column1, column2, ...
FROM table_name;

✅ Example:

sql
SELECT name, age
FROM students;

This retrieves the name and age columns from the students table.

🛠 Key Capabilities of SELECT:

  • Filter data using WHERE

  • Sort results with ORDER BY

  • Limit number of rows using LIMIT (or TOP in SQL Server)

  • Join multiple tables

  • Aggregate data using functions like SUM(), COUNT(), AVG()

  • Group results using GROUP BY

In summary, the SELECT statement is the most fundamental SQL command for reading and analyzing data in a relational database.

You said:
What is the function of an INSERT statement in SQL?
ChatGPT said:

The INSERT statement in SQL is used to add new rows (records) into a table.

✅ Function:

It inserts data into specified columns of a table in a database.

🧱 Basic Syntax:

sql
INSERT INTO table_name (column1, column2, ...)
VALUES (value1, value2, ...);

📌 Example:

sql
INSERT INTO employees (name, department, salary)
VALUES ('Alice', 'IT', 75000);

This adds a new employee named Alice to the employees table.

🛠 Key Variations:

  • Insert multiple rows at once:

    sql
    INSERT INTO students (name, age)
VALUES ('John', 20), ('Mary', 21), ('Ali', 22);

  • Insert into all columns (if you know the exact order):

    sql
    INSERT INTO products
VALUES (1, 'Phone', 300.00);

⚠️ Note:

Make sure the values match the data types and constraints (like NOT NULL, UNIQUE, etc.) defined in the table.

In summary, the INSERT statement is used to populate a table with new data.

You said:
What does 'atomicity' mean in the context of a database transaction?
ChatGPT said:

In the context of a database transaction, atomicity refers to the “all-or-nothing” principle.

✅ Definition:

Atomicity ensures that a transaction is treated as a single, indivisible unit of work.
This means that either all the operations in the transaction are completed successfully, or none of them are applied to the database.

🔍 Example:

Suppose you're transferring money between two bank accounts:

sql
-- Transaction Start
BEGIN;

UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE account_id = 1;  -- Debit
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE account_id = 2;  -- Credit

COMMIT;
-- Transaction End

If the first update (debit) succeeds but the second (credit) fails, atomicity ensures that the entire transaction is rolled back, so no money is lost or unaccounted for.

💡 Key Point:

Atomicity is the "A" in the ACID properties of transactions:

  • Atomicity

  • Consistency

  • Isolation

  • Durability

In short, atomicity guarantees data integrity by ensuring that partial transactions never affect the database.

Activity 1: Class with Inheritance (Smartphone example)

python
# Base class: ElectronicDevice
class ElectronicDevice:
    def __init__(self, brand, model, battery_life):
        self.brand = brand
        self.model = model
        self.battery_life = battery_life  # in hours

    def power_on(self):
        print(f"{self.brand} {self.model} is now ON.")

    def power_off(self):
        print(f"{self.brand} {self.model} is now OFF.")


# Derived class: Smartphone inherits from ElectronicDevice
class Smartphone(ElectronicDevice):
    def __init__(self, brand, model, battery_life, os, camera_megapixels):
        super().__init__(brand, model, battery_life)  # initialize base class attributes
        self.os = os
        self.camera_megapixels = camera_megapixels

    def take_photo(self):
        print(f"Taking a photo with {self.camera_megapixels}MP camera on {self.brand} {self.model}.")

    def install_app(self, app_name):
        print(f"Installing {app_name} on {self.os} smartphone.")


# Create objects
phone1 = Smartphone("Apple", "iPhone 14", 20, "iOS", 12)
phone2 = Smartphone("Samsung", "Galaxy S22", 24, "Android", 108)

# Use methods
phone1.power_on()
phone1.take_photo()
phone1.install_app("Instagram")
phone1.power_off()

print("---")

phone2.power_on()
phone2.take_photo()
phone2.install_app("WhatsApp")
phone2.power_off()

Activity 2: Polymorphism Challenge (Animals moving differently)

python
class Animal:
    def move(self):
        pass  # Abstract method to override


class Dog(Animal):
    def move(self):
        print("Running 🐕")


class Fish(Animal):
    def move(self):
        print("Swimming 🐟")


class Bird(Animal):
    def move(self):
        print("Flying 🐦")


# Create objects
dog = Dog()
fish = Fish()
bird = Bird()

# Polymorphism in action
for animal in (dog, fish, bird):
    animal.move()

Summary:

  • Activity 1 shows inheritance and encapsulation with shared and unique properties/methods.

  • Activity 2 shows polymorphism — same method name (move()) behaves differently depending on the class.

💻 Step 3: Load and Analyze in Python

python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the CSV file
df = pd.read_csv("sales_data.csv")

# Calculate total revenue
total_revenue = df["Revenue ($)"].sum()

# Best-selling product
best_product = df.groupby("Product")["Quantity Sold"].sum().idxmax()
best_qty = df.groupby("Product")["Quantity Sold"].sum().max()

# Highest sales day
top_day = df.groupby("Date")["Revenue ($)"].sum().idxmax()

# Create a summary DataFrame
summary_df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Metric": ["Total Revenue", "Best-Selling Product", "Units Sold", "Highest Sales Day"],
    "Value": [f"${total_revenue}", best_product, best_qty, top_day]
})

# Save summary to Excel
summary_df.to_excel("sales_summary.xlsx", index=False)

# Bonus: Plot sales trend and save it
df.groupby("Date")["Revenue ($)"].sum().plot(kind="line", marker="o", title="Daily Revenue Trend")
plt.xlabel("Date")
plt.ylabel("Revenue ($)")
plt.grid(True)

You said:
Which of the following is not a valid Django template tags?
ChatGPT said:

In Django, template tags are used within HTML templates to add logic, such as loops, conditions, and rendering variables. Let’s look at some valid template tags, and then identify the one that is not valid.

✅ Common Valid Django Template Tags:

  • {% if %} / {% endif %} – Conditional logic

  • {% for %} / {% endfor %} – Loops

  • {% block %} / {% endblock %} – Template inheritance

  • {% extends %} – Inherit from a parent template

  • {% include %} – Include another template

  • {% csrf_token %} – Add CSRF token for forms

  • {% url 'route_name' %} – Generate URLs from route names

❌ Not Valid (Examples):

Here are not valid Django template tags:

  • {% print %} – ❌ There’s no print tag in Django templates

  • {% function %} – ❌ Templates don't support raw Python functions

  • {% end %} – ❌ No such generic end tag; tags end with {% end<tagname> %}

  • {% variable %} – ❌ Variables use {{ variable }}, not {% variable %}

If you have a list of options, feel free to share them — I’ll tell you which one is not valid.

When you run the command:

Django automatically creates several files and folders inside the new app. Let’s look at which ones are included by default and which are not.

  • admin.py

  • models.py

  • tests.py

  • views.py

  • __init__.py

  • migrations/ (folder with __init__.py inside)

❌ Not Automatically Created:

Some common files not created automatically:

  • forms.py – ❌ You must create this manually if needed

  • urls.py – ❌ Also needs to be created manually

  • serializers.py – ❌ Used in Django REST Framework, not created by default

  • templates/ or static/ folders – ❌ Not automatically included

forms.py (or urls.py, if that’s among the options)

✅ Step-by-Step Guide to Analyzing Data with Pandas and Matplotlib

🔧 Step 1: Install Required Libraries

Open your terminal or command prompt and run:

📁 Step 2: Create a Python Script (data_analysis.py)

Copy and paste the following code into a file named data_analysis.py:

python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris

# Load Iris dataset
iris = load_iris(as_frame=True)
df = iris.frame

# Display the first 5 rows
print("First 5 rows of the dataset:")
print(df.head())

# Data types and missing values
print("\nData Types:")
print(df.dtypes)
print("\nMissing Values:")
print(df.isnull().sum())

# Describe statistics
print("\nDescriptive Statistics:")
print(df.describe())

# Group by species and mean
grouped = df.groupby("target").mean()
print("\nMean values grouped by species:")
print(grouped)

# Visualizations directory
output_dir = "."

# Line chart (simulate time-series)
df["date"] = pd.date_range(start="2025-01-01", periods=len(df))
time_series = df.groupby("date")["sepal length (cm)"].mean()
time_series.plot(title="Average Sepal Length Over Time")
plt.xlabel("Date")
plt.ylabel("Sepal Length (cm)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(f"{output_dir}/line_chart.png")
plt.clf()

# Bar chart
sns.barplot(x=iris.target_names, y=grouped["petal length (cm)"])
plt.title("Average Petal Length by Species")
plt.xlabel("Species")
plt.ylabel("Petal Length (cm)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(f"{output_dir}/bar_chart.png")
plt.clf()

# Histogram
plt.hist(df["sepal width (cm)"], bins=20, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black')
plt.title("Distribution of Sepal Width")
plt.xlabel("Sepal Width (cm)")
plt.ylabel("Count")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(f"{output_dir}/histogram.png")
plt.clf()

# Scatter plot
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x="sepal length (cm)", y="petal length (cm)", hue="target", palette="Set2")
plt.title("Sepal Length vs Petal Length")
plt.xlabel("Sepal Length (cm)")
plt.ylabel("Petal Length (cm)")
plt.legend(title="Species", labels=iris.target_names)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(f"{output_dir}/scatter_plot.png")
plt.clf()

print("\nAll plots saved successfully!")

📈 Step 3: Run the Script

bash
python data_analysis.py

It will:

  • Print insights to the console

  • Save the charts as line_chart.png, bar_chart.png, histogram.png, and scatter_plot.png in your current directory.
